findings.title: AI whole-command retry can discard pending caller changes
findings.trigger: A PostgreSQL Recovery command enters with caller-owned tracked pending changes and no EF CurrentTransaction, then its owned attempt receives native 40001 or 40P01. The helper clears the whole tracker and may return a successful idempotency replay on its next attempt, silently losing pending caller changes.
findings.reason: SpaceAiOwnedCommandRetry excludes only CurrentTransaction. Recovery methods do not clear caller changes at entry. There is no HasChanges or ambient/enlisted eligibility check, unlike the existing EditLease retry wrapper.
findings.acceptedFix: Use the EditLease eligibility boundary: pending changes or EF/ambient/enlisted caller transactions keep the original single operation path, without new whole-command retry or tracker clearing.
findings.statusAtInitialReview: Confirmed by root; fix and native regression pending.

checks: PostgreSQL snapshot clone matches retained SQL Server batch column lists, copy order, tenant/soft-delete conditions and source/calibration/element remapping for twelve tables.
Clone stays within caller transaction. Distinct invocation map names, ON COMMIT DROP and explicit success cleanup retain the intended rollback boundary.
New clone edge tests use a real final-table CHECK, two physical sessions and a SaveChanges barrier; they assert full rollback, source fingerprints, temporary map cleanup and scheduled retry.

Capacity and file retry boundaries cover complete owned database transactions. Budget empty intervals receive a tenant transaction resource lock. External object operations are outside replayed commands.
AI Run/Version/Model row locks explicitly scope tenant and entity. Worker external effects are not wrapped by the newly added command retry helper.
Relevant native test changes preserve business assertions and provider-specific native failure evidence; original failed batches are retained rather than relabeled as a single green matrix.
